raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year on my 5 mu.

---

Been farming this same patch for twenty years, took it on when I married into the village. Five mu isn't much so I have to think carefully — every yuan matters when the farm is this small. My husband works in town most of the year, comes back for the busy times. Our two kids are still in school so I can't count on them much except on weekends and in summer.

I split my land like this: three mu I do wheat-maize back to back, that's my staple system. One mu cotton, one mu peanut. The wheat-maize on the three mu gives us our grain to eat and some to sell. Cotton is the cash crop — prices go up and down but it's been okay. Peanut I keep partly because we eat it, partly because it's easy on the land and doesn't need much fertilizer — something about the bumps on the roots, the extension guy explained it once.

**Wheat (already in the ground since October).** I put down about one and a half bags of 15-15-15 compound per mu before I plowed — that's around 75 kg of compound. Topdressed urea in early April when it was jointing, maybe 15-17 kg to the mu. Winter watering once, jointing once, probably one more before flowering. Last year I got 430 kg per mu — a late cold snap hurt me a bit. This year the winter was alright, I'm hoping for 440-450. I'll hire the combine in June, about 80 yuan a mu, not worth doing by hand.

**Maize — goes in right after wheat comes off in mid-June.** That turnaround week is the hardest time of year. I hire the combine for wheat, and the same day or next I hire a no-till planter to put the maize in. Hybrid seed, about 60 yuan a mu — I don't save maize seed, the hybrids don't come back true. I put compound down with the seed, then topdress urea when it's knee-high. Two waterings usually, maybe three if July is dry. I expect around 450 kg per mu — maize has been consistent for me.

**Cotton — planting in about a week or two when the soil warms.** I use Bt hybrid, about 80 yuan a mu — expensive but I can't afford to lose it to bollworm. I do a proper plow, put down compound at planting, topdress when it's flowering. Water once or twice. The real work with cotton is picking — starts in September and goes into October. My sister helps me for two weeks, otherwise I can't manage. I'm aiming for around 240 kg lint per mu, depending on whether it's a wet autumn.

**Peanut goes in early May.** I saved seed from last year's crop — saves me money. Peanut doesn't need much nitrogen so I just put down a half-bag of compound per mu at planting. One watering during flowering if it's dry. My daughter-in-law from the village helps me pick in September. I expect maybe 240-250 kg per mu.

Total costs for the year, I'm reckoning around 2,800 yuan across the five mu. It's tight. If cotton has a bad year I'll lean harder on the wheat-maize.
